check_text:
protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 errors, 2 notes).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: dye (well A1 in slot 2)
   line 28:  p300.aspirate(5, dye_plate["A1"])
   At line 28 the tip went into dye (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried sample 1
   (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4
   (well A4 in slot 1) and 7 more from an earlier step (this line did it 11 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3
   more in slot 1.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 28 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [0a95c4c45db8]

2. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 28:  p300.aspirate(5, dye_plate["A1"])
   At line 28 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 12 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: well A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [6fc4964e87b0]

3. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 28:  p300.aspirate(5, dye_plate["A1"])
   At line 28 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 2 while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 7 more from an earlier step (this line did it 11 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 1.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 28, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [07ae6883403c]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 12 wells never mixed after dye went in (25% of the well)
   line 29:  p300.dispense(5, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 29 the robot added dye to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot
   1, which already held sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more (this line did it
   12 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the
   run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their
   own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is
   vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the
   instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 1 after line 29:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [f8000a11ddf8]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 28 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 28 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 12 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: well A1 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 28 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 2 while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 1), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 1), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 1), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 1) and 7 more from an earlier step (this line did it 11 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 28, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: 12 wells never mixed after dye went in (25% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 29 the robot added dye to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 1, which already held sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 8 more (this line did it 12 times). The addition was 25% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 1 after line 29: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
